Owner decision 1 (2026-10-06): Gutenberg texts (canModify: false) are not adapted; this is a NEW course-authored text, with no plot or wording borrowed from the work named in PLAN-B1. (Niebla ch22; the unit sits at slot 27 so that the Martí chapter that profits from its farm vocabulary comes after it.) A new rural story with dialogue; characters and plot are invented. Points for the Honduran reviewer: usted between neighbours and elders (voseo is not used here on purpose), "alcalde auxiliar", "pulpería", "milpa", "chala" (corn husk, for tamales), "cipotes", "arado" (ploughing with a buey), "niebla" in the mountains, the wording of the funeral and the condolence note. Owner decision 3: the 92 % entry line for authentic placements stays; new-lemmas warnings are acceptable. sentences.text: En las montañas de Honduras, la niebla baja cada mañana hasta las casas y no se va hasta que sale el sol.
sentences.english: In the mountains of Honduras the fog comes down every morning as far as the houses and does not go until the sun comes up.

sentences.text: Aquella mañana la niebla cubría todo más que nunca, y la aldea parecía una isla dentro de una nube.
sentences.english: That morning the fog covered everything more than ever, and the village looked like an island inside a cloud.

sentences.text: Doña Aurora salió al patio con una taza de café y miró hacia el sendero que cruzaba su terreno.
sentences.english: Doña Aurora went out into the yard with a cup of coffee and looked towards the path that crossed her land.

sentences.text: Hacía una semana que había enterrado a su marido, y todavía no se acostumbraba al silencio de la casa.
sentences.english: It was a week since she had buried her husband, and she still had not got used to the silence of the house.

sentences.text: Era viuda desde el lunes pasado, y el entierro había sido el más largo que la aldea recordaba.
sentences.english: She had been a widow since last Monday, and the funeral had been the longest the village could remember.

sentences.text: Todos habían venido al entierro: los vecinos, los niños de la escuela y hasta el pastor de la otra aldea.
sentences.english: Everyone had come to the funeral: the neighbours, the schoolchildren and even the pastor from the other village.

sentences.text: Cada vecino había traído un ramo de flores, y el ramo más grande era el de los niños de la escuela.
sentences.english: Each neighbour had brought a bunch of flowers, and the biggest bunch was the one from the schoolchildren.

sentences.text: Sobre la tumba todavía quedaba un ramo seco, y doña Aurora no se atrevía a quitarlo.
sentences.english: On the grave there was still a dry bunch, and doña Aurora did not dare to remove it.

sentences.text: Sólo faltó una persona, y esa persona era don Miguel.
sentences.english: Only one person was missing, and that person was don Miguel.

sentences.text: Nadie sabía por qué no había venido, y todo se complicó con eso.
sentences.english: Nobody knew why he had not come, and everything got complicated because of it.

sentences.text: Don Miguel era un anciano solterón, y vivía solo en la casa de arriba, al otro lado del sendero.
sentences.english: Don Miguel was an old bachelor, and he lived alone in the house above, on the other side of the path.

sentences.text: Los vecinos decían que un solterón de su edad ya no tenía nada que esperar, pero él nunca contestaba.
sentences.english: The neighbours said that a bachelor of his age had nothing left to look forward to, but he never answered.

sentences.text: Era un anciano melancólico, y tenía la costumbre de callar cuando algo le dolía.
sentences.english: He was a melancholy old man, and he had the habit of keeping quiet when something hurt him.

sentences.text: Un hombre melancólico como él no pide nada, y por eso nadie le daba nada.
sentences.english: A melancholy man like him asks for nothing, and that is why nobody gave him anything.

sentences.text: Cada mañana bajaba por el sendero con su arado al hombro, y cruzaba el terreno de doña Aurora para llegar a su milpa.
sentences.english: Every morning he went down the path with his plough on his shoulder, and crossed doña Aurora's land to reach his cornfield.

sentences.text: Delante del arado caminaba su buey, un animal viejo que tenía un cuerno roto y el espinazo delgado.
sentences.english: In front of the plough walked his ox, an old animal with a broken horn and a thin backbone.

sentences.text: Cuando el buey se cansaba, don Miguel le tocaba el espinazo y le hablaba bajito.
sentences.english: When the ox got tired, don Miguel touched its backbone and spoke softly to it.

sentences.text: Por la noche el buey dormía en el corral de la casa de arriba, y don Miguel le miraba el cuerno antes de acostarse.
sentences.english: At night the ox slept in the pen of the house above, and don Miguel looked at its horn before going to bed.

sentences.text: Los cipotes se escondían a veces en el corral de doña Aurora para ver pasar al buey.
sentences.english: The kids sometimes hid in doña Aurora's yard pen to watch the ox go by.

sentences.text: También el corral de doña Aurora estaba vacío desde la muerte de su marido, y el cerro parecía más callado.
sentences.english: Doña Aurora's pen had also been empty since her husband's death, and the hill seemed quieter.

sentences.text: Allí, entre la niebla, empujaba el arado con un ritmo lento y seguro, y la tierra se abría como un libro.
sentences.english: There, in the fog, he pushed the plough with a slow, sure rhythm, and the earth opened like a book.

sentences.text: Su trabajo parecía inútil a los jóvenes, que querían ir a la ciudad y no sembrar nada.
sentences.english: His work seemed useless to the young people, who wanted to go to the city and not sow anything.

sentences.text: Un par de cipotes se reían de él, y le decían que su arado era inútil.
sentences.english: A couple of kids laughed at him, and told him his plough was useless.

sentences.text: Don Miguel los miraba con un aire melancólico, y seguía arando al mismo ritmo.
sentences.english: Don Miguel looked at them with a melancholy air, and went on ploughing at the same rhythm.

sentences.text: Pero para don Miguel, el ritmo del arado era una oración, y la milpa era lo único interesante que le quedaba.
sentences.english: But for don Miguel the rhythm of the plough was a prayer, and the cornfield was the only interesting thing he had left.

sentences.text: Para un anciano solterón no hay nada más interesante que una tierra que responde, y su milpa le respondía.
sentences.english: For an old bachelor there is nothing more interesting than land that answers, and his cornfield answered him.

sentences.text: Nadie en la aldea recordaba cuándo había empezado esa costumbre, y nadie le había preguntado nunca por qué.
sentences.english: Nobody in the village remembered when that custom had begun, and nobody had ever asked him why.

sentences.text: Pero esa semana corrió un rumor: doña Aurora, ahora que era viuda, iba a cerrar el sendero.
sentences.english: But that week a rumour went round: doña Aurora, now that she was a widow, was going to close the path.

sentences.text: El rumor llegó a la pulpería, y de la pulpería llegó a oídos de don Miguel.
sentences.english: The rumour reached the shop, and from the shop it reached don Miguel's ears.

sentences.text: —Dicen que la viuda va a poner una cerca —dijo la dueña de la pulpería—.
sentences.english: "They say the widow is going to put up a fence," said the owner of the shop.

sentences.text: —Eso es un rumor, y nada más —contestó don Carlos, el alcalde auxiliar—.
sentences.english: "That is a rumour, and nothing more," answered don Carlos, the local mayor.

sentences.text: —Un rumor es como el fuego en la chala seca —dijo la dueña—.
sentences.english: "A rumour is like fire in dry corn husks," said the owner.

sentences.text: —Si cae en la chala, todo se quema, y no hay autoridad que lo apague.
sentences.english: "If it falls on the husks, everything burns, and no authority can put it out."

sentences.text: —Ya vimos lo que pasa cuando un rumor se vuelve tragedia —dijo don Carlos—.
sentences.english: "We have already seen what happens when a rumour turns into a tragedy," said don Carlos.

sentences.text: —Hace diez años, por un rumor, dos familias dejaron de hablarse para siempre.
sentences.english: "Ten years ago, because of a rumour, two families stopped speaking to each other for ever."

sentences.text: —Todo rumor necesita un pretexto, y este todavía no lo sabemos.
sentences.english: "Every rumour needs a pretext, and we do not know this one yet."

sentences.text: —El pretexto de un rumor casi siempre es un negocio, don Carlos, y no digo más.
sentences.english: "The pretext for a rumour is almost always a deal, don Carlos, and I will say no more."

sentences.text: —No es una tragedia todavía, pero puede serlo.
sentences.english: "It is not a tragedy yet, but it could become one."

sentences.text: Don Miguel escuchó todo desde un rincón de la pulpería, y no dijo nada.
sentences.english: Don Miguel listened to everything from a corner of the shop and said nothing.

sentences.text: Esa noche no durmió, y por la mañana bajó por el sendero con el arado y con una rabia que no era suya.
sentences.english: That night he did not sleep, and in the morning he went down the path with the plough and with an anger that was not really his.

sentences.text: Doña Aurora lo vio llegar entre la niebla y comprendió todo de golpe.
sentences.english: Doña Aurora saw him coming through the fog and understood everything at once.

sentences.text: El anciano no se movió del sendero, y se quedó aterrado, con el arado en la mano.
sentences.english: The old man did not move from the path, and stood terrified, with the plough in his hand.

sentences.text: —Buenos días, don Miguel —dijo, sin moverse de la puerta—.
sentences.english: "Good morning, don Miguel," she said, without moving from the door.

sentences.text: —No tienen nada de buenos, doña Aurora —contestó él—.
sentences.english: "They are not good at all, doña Aurora," he answered.

sentences.text: —Me dijeron que usted iba a cerrar el sendero, y que lo iba a cerrar ahora mismo.
sentences.english: "They told me you were going to close the path, and that you were going to close it right now."

sentences.text: —¿Y usted lo creyó?
sentences.english: "And you believed it?"

sentences.text: —Yo no sé qué creer.
sentences.english: "I don't know what to believe."

sentences.text: —Treinta años crucé este terreno, y ahora me entero por un rumor.
sentences.english: "I have crossed this land for thirty years, and now I find out through a rumour."

sentences.text: La voz de don Miguel temblaba, y doña Aurora vio que el viejo estaba aterrado.
sentences.english: Don Miguel's voice trembled, and doña Aurora saw that the old man was terrified.

sentences.text: No tenía miedo de ella, sino de perder lo único que le quedaba: el camino hacia su milpa.
sentences.english: He was not afraid of her but of losing the only thing he had left: the road to his cornfield.

sentences.text: Estaba aterrado, y en su interior sentía una rabia vieja que no sabía cómo decir.
sentences.english: He was terrified, and inside him he felt an old anger that he did not know how to put into words.

sentences.text: En su interior, doña Aurora sentía lo mismo: una tristeza que no sabía cómo decir.
sentences.english: Inside, doña Aurora felt the same: a sadness she did not know how to put into words.

sentences.text: En el interior de la casa, el café ya estaba frío.
sentences.english: Inside the house, the coffee was already cold.

sentences.text: —Don Miguel, yo no tolero que se hable así de mí en la aldea —dijo ella—.
sentences.english: "Don Miguel, I will not tolerate people talking about me like that in the village," she said.

sentences.text: —Tampoco tolero la grosería, y menos en un día como éste.
sentences.english: "Nor do I tolerate rudeness, and least of all on a day like this."

sentences.text: —Y no voy a tolerar que nadie nos separe por un rumor.
sentences.english: "And I am not going to tolerate anyone separating us over a rumour."

sentences.text: —Pero tampoco voy a pelear con usted, y no le voy a decir una grosería.
sentences.english: "But neither am I going to fight with you, and I am not going to say a rude word to you."

sentences.text: —Si yo estallo, usted estalla, y la aldea se pierde completamente.
sentences.english: "If I explode, you explode, and the village is completely lost."

sentences.text: —Completamente, don Miguel: esto no puede seguir así.
sentences.english: "Completely, don Miguel: this cannot go on like this."

sentences.text: —¿Quién le dijo eso de la cerca?
sentences.english: "Who told you that about the fence?"

sentences.text: —Fue una de las mujeres de la pulpería.
sentences.english: "It was one of the women at the shop."

sentences.text: —Dijo que se lo contó un sobrino suyo.
sentences.english: "She said a nephew of yours told her."

sentences.text: —Un sobrino mío —repitió doña Aurora, y se quedó callada un momento—.
sentences.english: "A nephew of mine," repeated doña Aurora, and she was quiet for a moment.

sentences.text: —Entonces ya sé quién fue.
sentences.english: "Then I know who it was."

sentences.text: Esa tarde, don Carlos, el alcalde auxiliar, llamó a todos a la pulpería.
sentences.english: That afternoon don Carlos, the local mayor, called everyone to the shop.

sentences.text: Don Miguel vino, y vino también doña Aurora, con su sobrino Luis detrás de ella.
sentences.english: Don Miguel came, and doña Aurora came too, with her nephew Luis behind her.

sentences.text: Luis tenía veinte años, y no parecía contento de estar allí.
sentences.english: Luis was twenty, and he did not look happy to be there.

sentences.text: Todo se complicó más cuando Luis entró, porque nadie sabía qué hacer con él.
sentences.english: Everything got more complicated when Luis came in, because nobody knew what to do with him.

sentences.text: —Perdonen la molestia —dijo don Carlos, que sabía mantener la calma—.
sentences.english: "Forgive the trouble," said don Carlos, who knew how to keep calm.

sentences.text: Pidió perdón por la molestia otra vez, porque sabía que nadie quería estar allí.
sentences.english: He apologised for the trouble again, because he knew that nobody wanted to be there.

sentences.text: —Soy la autoridad de la aldea, y estoy a la disposición de todos ustedes, pero esto se está complicando.
sentences.english: "I am the authority of the village, and I am at everyone's disposal, but this is getting complicated."

sentences.text: La autoridad de don Carlos no venía de su cargo, sino de su manera de escuchar, y su disposición se notaba.
sentences.english: Don Carlos's authority did not come from his post but from his way of listening, and his readiness showed.

sentences.text: —Alguien dijo que doña Aurora iba a cerrar el sendero, y la cosa se complicó.
sentences.english: "Someone said that doña Aurora was going to close the path, and things got complicated."

sentences.text: —No quiero destruir a nadie, y tampoco quiero confundir las cosas: primero hablamos y después decidimos.
sentences.english: "I do not want to destroy anybody, and I do not want to mix things up either: first we talk and then we decide."

sentences.text: —Yo quiero saber quién lo dijo y para qué.
sentences.english: "I want to know who said it and what for."

sentences.text: Luis miró el piso, y por fin habló, confundido y con la voz baja.
sentences.english: Luis looked at the floor, and at last he spoke, confused and in a low voice.

sentences.text: —Fui yo, tía —dijo—.
sentences.english: "It was me, aunt," he said.

sentences.text: —Yo pensé que si la gente creía que usted iba a cerrar el sendero, usted ya no iba a poder venderlo.
sentences.english: "I thought that if people believed you were going to close the path, you would no longer be able to sell it."

sentences.text: —¿Vender qué? —preguntó doña Aurora, sorprendida.
sentences.english: "Sell what?" asked doña Aurora, surprised.

sentences.text: —El terreno, tía.
sentences.english: "The land, aunt."

sentences.text: —Un señor de la ciudad quiere comprarlo, y me dijo que me iba a dar una ganancia.
sentences.english: "A man from the city wants to buy it, and he told me he would give me a cut."

sentences.text: —Pero usted nunca me preguntó si quería vender.
sentences.english: "But you never asked me if I wanted to sell."

sentences.text: —No le pregunté porque pensé que usted iba a decir que no.
sentences.english: "I didn't ask because I thought you would say no."

sentences.text: —Y tenías razón —contestó ella—.
sentences.english: "And you were right," she answered.

sentences.text: —Usted usó la muerte de mi marido como un pretexto, y ese pretexto me dolió más que el negocio.
sentences.english: "You used my husband's death as a pretext, and that pretext hurt me more than the deal."

sentences.text: Luis había confundido un negocio con un favor, y ahora toda la aldea lo sabía.
sentences.english: Luis had mistaken a deal for a favour, and now the whole village knew it.

sentences.text: Era un joven confundido, y se sentía completamente solo en medio de la pulpería.
sentences.english: He was a confused young man, and he felt completely alone in the middle of the shop.

sentences.text: Él mismo ya no sabía si había buscado un pretexto o una razón, y no sabía qué era más interesante: callar o hablar.
sentences.english: He himself no longer knew whether he had looked for a pretext or a reason, and he did not know which was more interesting: to be silent or to speak.

sentences.text: Nadie dijo una grosería, pero el silencio fue peor que un grito.
sentences.english: Nobody said a rude word, but the silence was worse than a shout.

sentences.text: Entonces doña Aurora se puso de pie, y todos esperaron que estallara.
sentences.english: Then doña Aurora stood up, and everyone expected her to explode.

sentences.text: Pero habló con una voz tranquila, la voz de una mujer que ya había llorado mucho.
sentences.english: But she spoke in a quiet voice, the voice of a woman who had already cried a lot.

sentences.text: —Este terreno era de mi marido, y mi marido nunca cerró el sendero —dijo—.
sentences.english: "This land was my husband's, and my husband never closed the path," she said.

sentences.text: —No lo voy a cerrar yo tampoco, y menos para que lo destruyan con una casa de ciudad.
sentences.english: "I am not going to close it either, and least of all so that they can ruin it with a city house."

sentences.text: —Es un terreno pequeño, pero destruirlo sería una tragedia.
sentences.english: "It is a small piece of land, but destroying it would be a tragedy."

sentences.text: —Don Miguel, el sendero es suyo, y de todos los que lo necesiten.
sentences.english: "Don Miguel, the path is yours, and everybody's who needs it."

sentences.text: —Mi casa y mi terreno están a su disposición, y no son una molestia para mí.
sentences.english: "My house and my land are at your disposal, and they are no trouble to me."

sentences.text: —No ha sido nunca una molestia, don Miguel, y nunca lo fue.
sentences.english: "You have never been a bother, don Miguel, and never were."

sentences.text: Don Miguel bajó la cabeza, y por primera vez en treinta años no supo qué decir.
sentences.english: Don Miguel bowed his head, and for the first time in thirty years he did not know what to say.

sentences.text: Sacó del bolsillo un lápiz pequeño y un papel doblado, y escribió algo con una mano que temblaba.
sentences.english: He took a small pencil and a folded paper from his pocket, and wrote something with a hand that trembled.

sentences.text: Después le dio el papel a doña Aurora, y ella lo leyó en voz alta: «Gracias por el entierro de su marido, que yo no pude ver porque me dio miedo».
sentences.english: Then he gave the paper to doña Aurora, and she read it aloud: "Thank you for your husband's funeral, which I could not see because I was afraid."

sentences.text: —¿Miedo de qué, don Miguel? —preguntó ella—.
sentences.english: "Afraid of what, don Miguel?" she asked.

sentences.text: —Nadie debe tener miedo de llorar a un amigo.
sentences.english: "Nobody should be afraid of mourning a friend."

sentences.text: —De que usted pensara que yo era un par de pies que cruzaban su terreno, y nada más.
sentences.english: "That you might think I was just a pair of feet crossing your land, and nothing more."

sentences.text: —Sólo un par de pies, y un solterón sin nada.
sentences.english: "Just a pair of feet, and a bachelor with nothing."

sentences.text: —Usted fue siempre más que eso —dijo ella—.
sentences.english: "You were always more than that," she said.

sentences.text: —Mi marido hablaba de usted cada vez que llovía, y decía que no había nadie que supiera mejor cuándo sembrar.
sentences.english: "My husband talked about you every time it rained, and said that nobody knew better when to sow."

sentences.text: Al día siguiente, la niebla bajó otra vez, y don Miguel cruzó el sendero con el arado al hombro, como siempre.
sentences.english: The next day the fog came down again, and don Miguel crossed the path with the plough on his shoulder, as always.

sentences.text: Pero esta vez se detuvo en la puerta y dejó mucha chala seca, de la que se usa para envolver tamales.
sentences.english: But this time he stopped at the door and left a lot of dry corn husks, the kind used for wrapping tamales.

sentences.text: Doña Aurora entendió el mensaje, y esa tarde envolvió tamales en la chala para toda la aldea.
sentences.english: Doña Aurora understood the message, and that afternoon she wrapped tamales in the husks for the whole village.

sentences.text: Don Miguel fue el primero en comer, y el último en irse.
sentences.english: Don Miguel was the first to eat, and the last to leave.

sentences.text: Luis lavó los platos, sin que nadie se lo pidiera, y cuando salió, el sendero se veía claro bajo el sol de la tarde.
sentences.english: Luis washed the dishes without anyone asking him to, and when he went out the path looked bright under the afternoon sun.

sentences.text: Cuando el albergue cerró, Karla, Sam y Yesenia subieron al cerro para visitar a doña Aurora.
sentences.english: When the shelter closed, Karla, Sam and Yesenia went up the hill to visit doña Aurora.

sentences.text: Llevaban cobijas, una campaña de ayuda en un papel, y un suero para los niños, porque la creciente también había llegado hasta allá arriba.
sentences.english: They carried blankets, an aid campaign on a paper, and a serum for the children, because the flood had also reached up there.

sentences.text: —Le aconsejo, señora, que hierva el agua —dijo Karla—. La enfermera lo dice en su crónica.
sentences.english: "I advise you, ma'am, to boil the water," said Karla. "The nurse says it in her chronicle."

sentences.text: —Muy bien, mija —contestó doña Aurora—. Aquí, de repente, llueve más de la cuenta, y el terreno se hace barro.
sentences.english: "Very good, my dear," answered doña Aurora. "Here, suddenly, it rains more than it should, and the ground turns to mud."

sentences.text: Yesenia, que llevaba una ficha con los datos de cada familia, preguntó cuántos vivían en la casa.
sentences.english: Yesenia, who carried a card with the data of each family, asked how many lived in the house.

sentences.text: —Tres, y un preso que volvió ayer —dijo la señora, y bajó la voz—. Estaba en la cárcel, pero con el agua lo trasladaron.
sentences.english: "Three, and a prisoner who came back yesterday," said the lady, and lowered her voice. "He was in jail, but with the water they moved him."

sentences.text: —Yo no me enteré de nada —dijo Sam—. ¿Es él?
sentences.english: "I didn't find out about anything," said Sam. "Is it him?"

sentences.text: Un joven pálido, sentado junto al fogón, levantó la mirada. Su voz era un susurro, y su temor, evidente.
sentences.english: A pale young man, sitting by the stove, raised his gaze. His voice was a whisper, and his fear, evident.

sentences.text: —No quiero un castigo más —dijo—. Quiero un testigo que cuente lo acontecido, y un encuentro con mi madre.
sentences.english: "I don't want one more punishment," he said. "I want a witness who tells what happened, and a meeting with my mother."

sentences.text: —Mi hijo no es un capricho de la desgracia —repuso doña Aurora, sin ofender a nadie—. Es un hombre que se perdió.
sentences.english: "My son is not a whim of misfortune," replied doña Aurora, without offending anyone. "He is a man who got lost."

sentences.text: Sam se sentó a su lado. No quería hablar de religión ni de moral; solo quería acompañar con sencillez.
sentences.english: Sam sat beside him. He didn't want to talk about religion or morals; he only wanted to accompany with simplicity.

sentences.text: —Estaba espantado, y me atormentaba el recuerdo de aquel azote —dijo el joven—. Pero ahora, con esta tranquilidad, todo es distinto.
sentences.english: "I was frightened, and the memory of that lash tormented me," said the young man. "But now, with this calm, everything is different."

sentences.text: Una nube blanca bajó sobre el cerro, y un relámpago iluminó la cocina por un segundo. Nadie se asustó.
sentences.english: A white cloud came down on the hill, and a flash of lightning lit the kitchen for a second. Nobody got scared.

sentences.text: —Una experta de la clínica nos habló de las víctimas —dijo Karla—. Aconseja que no se entre al río mientras la creciente sea profunda.
sentences.english: "An expert from the clinic told us about the victims," said Karla. "She advises that people not enter the river while the flood is deep."

sentences.text: —Los damnificados necesitan donaciones, pero sobre todo compañía —añadió Yesenia, que había escrito una entrevista con el alcalde—. Y los voluntarios, un compromiso real.
sentences.english: "The victims need donations, but above all company," added Yesenia, who had written an interview with the mayor. "And the volunteers, a real commitment."

sentences.text: En un rincón, unos niños inquietos y agitados dibujaban en un mural de plástico. Una niña pintó una flecha que apuntaba al cielo.
sentences.english: In a corner, some restless and agitated children drew on a plastic mural. A girl painted an arrow pointing to the sky.

sentences.text: —¿Qué dice la flecha? —preguntó Sam.
sentences.english: "What does the arrow say?" asked Sam.

sentences.text: —Que no hay desastre perfecto —contestó la niña—. Siempre hay alguien que rozó una mano.
sentences.english: "That there is no perfect disaster," the girl answered. "There is always somebody who touched a hand."

sentences.text: Sam sonrió. La paciencia de esa niña le parecía la más admirada de todas, aunque ella no lo sabía.
sentences.english: Sam smiled. That girl's patience seemed to him the most admired of all, although she did not know it.

sentences.text: Mientras tomaban café, doña Aurora contó que su difunto marido había sido un artista, un hombre de poca timidez y mucha literatura.
sentences.english: While they drank coffee, doña Aurora told that her late husband had been an artist, a man of little shyness and much literature.

sentences.text: —Él decía que un servicio sin cadena es un servicio sincero —recordó ella—. Que la ayuda no debe ofender, y que el estómago lleno no sirve si el apetito del alma está vacío.
sentences.english: "He used to say that a service without a chain is a sincere service," she remembered. "That help must not offend, and that a full stomach is no good if the appetite of the soul is empty."

sentences.text: Antes de bajar, Karla dejó una ambulancia de juguete para el nieto de la señora, y Yesenia una ficha con el teléfono de la clínica.
sentences.english: Before going down, Karla left a toy ambulance for the lady's grandson, and Yesenia a card with the clinic's phone number.

sentences.text: —La consulta es gratuita —explicó—. No necesita carné ni apellido, y la entrada está siempre abierta.
sentences.english: "The consultation is free," she explained. "It needs neither a card nor a surname, and the entrance is always open."

sentences.text: —Está prohibido fumar, pero la salida de emergencia es amplia —bromeó Sam, y todos se rieron.
sentences.english: "Smoking is prohibited, but the emergency exit is wide," joked Sam, and everybody laughed.

sentences.text: Al salir, el joven apretó la mano de Sam con firmeza, y no dijo nada más.
sentences.english: On leaving, the young man squeezed Sam's hand firmly and said nothing more.

sentences.text: En el camino de regreso, Yesenia dijo que ese día había entendido el rigor de la compasión, y el valor de una dosis pequeña de esperanza.
sentences.english: On the way back, Yesenia said that that day she had understood the rigor of compassion, and the value of a small dose of hope.

sections.title: Palabras para repasar con doña Aurora

sentences.text: Esa noche, doña Aurora y sus visitas repasaron en voz alta las palabras de las últimas semanas.
sentences.english: That night, doña Aurora and her visitors went over aloud the words of the last weeks.

sentences.text: —¿Qué es un testigo? —Es una persona que cuenta lo acontecido, aunque esté alarmada y sienta suspenso.
sentences.english: "What is a witness?" "It is a person who tells what happened, even if she is alarmed and feels suspense."

sentences.text: —¿Y qué hace una persona admirada? —Pone su paciencia en el trabajo y su literatura en la mesa, y ni siquiera lo sabe.
sentences.english: "And what does an admired person do?" "She puts her patience into work and her literature on the table, and does not even know it."

sentences.text: —¿Quién empujó la puerta? —Nadie la empujó; el viento la empujó.
sentences.english: "Who pushed the door?" "Nobody pushed it; the wind pushed it."

sentences.text: —¿Dónde nacen los zancudos? —En el agua quieta de un criadero. Hay que vaciar cada criadero, y hay que vaciar los criaderos del patio.
sentences.english: "Where are mosquitoes born?" "In the standing water of a breeding place. Every breeding place must be emptied, and the breeding places of the yard too."

sentences.text: —¿Cómo se llama al que está en la cárcel? —Preso. Los presos fueron trasladados a la escuela, y los trasladados esperaron allí.
sentences.english: "What do you call someone who is in jail?" "Prisoner. The prisoners were moved to the school, and those who were moved waited there."

sentences.text: —¿Es profundo ese río? —Sí, es profundo, y el agua no es potable sin cloro.
sentences.english: "Is that river deep?" "Yes, it is deep, and the water is not drinkable without chlorine."

sentences.text: —¿Cuándo se atiende a un enfermo grave? —Inmediatamente. Un niño agitado no puede esperar.
sentences.english: "When is a seriously ill person attended to?" "Immediately. An agitated child cannot wait."

sentences.text: —¿Qué necesita una campaña de ayuda? —Una preparación cuidadosa, pasos concretos y alguien que pueda justificar cada gasto.
sentences.english: "What does an aid campaign need?" "Careful preparation, concrete steps and somebody who can justify each expense."

sentences.text: —¿Y quién solicitó una entrevista? —Los vecinos la solicitaron, y el alcalde dijo que sí. Los vecinos solicitaron también un pañuelo para cada niño.
sentences.english: "And who requested an interview?" "The neighbours requested it, and the mayor said yes. The neighbours also requested a handkerchief for each child."

sentences.text: —¿Cómo se llena una ficha? —Con la identidad de la persona, su firma y su apellido. Es urgente, pero nunca formalmente complicada.
sentences.english: "How is a card filled out?" "With the person's identity, signature and surname. It is urgent, but never formally complicated."

sentences.text: —¿Qué lleva un voluntario? —Guantes, un litro de agua, una cucharada de azúcar y una gota de paciencia.
sentences.english: "What does a volunteer carry?" "Gloves, a liter of water, a spoonful of sugar and a drop of patience."

sentences.text: —¿Está comprometido el voluntario? —Sí, está comprometido y enterado. Todo es excelente, si el trabajo es habitual y limpio, no sucio.
sentences.english: "Is the volunteer committed?" "Yes, he is committed and informed. Everything is excellent, if the work is habitual and clean, not dirty."

sentences.text: —¿Quién se sienta en las butacas? —Los espectadores. Cuando la sala está iluminada, nadie se alarma. Cuando la sala exige silencio, hay silencio.
sentences.english: "Who sits in the seats?" "The spectators. When the room is lit, nobody is alarmed. When the room demands silence, there is silence."

sentences.text: —¿Dónde se guardan las latas de comida? —En el almacén, en cajas, bajo una luz iluminada.
sentences.english: "Where are the cans of food kept?" "In the storeroom, in boxes, under a lit light."

sentences.text: —¿Y los condiscípulos? —Son los compañeros de clase. Ellos se contuvieron para no gritar, y los saciados no se quejaron.
sentences.english: "And the schoolmates?" "They are the classmates. They held back so as not to shout, and the full ones did not complain."

sentences.text: —¿Qué es una ceremonia? —Es un acto con orden: nadie es inutilón, y hasta los furiosos aprenden a contenerse.
sentences.english: "What is a ceremony?" "It is an act with order: nobody is useless, and even the furious learn to hold back."

sentences.text: —¿Cómo se consuela a los turbados? —Con una palabra tranquila de la Biblia: «No os entristezcáis».
sentences.english: "How are the troubled ones comforted?" "With a calm word from the Bible: 'Do not be sad.'"

sentences.text: —¿Cómo se agradece un favor? —Con agradecimiento y con modales finos, sin disgusto y sin palabras amargas.
sentences.english: "How is a favor thanked?" "With gratitude and with fine manners, without displeasure and without bitter words."

sentences.text: —¿Y qué hace un yerno? —Un yerno ayuda a su suegra, y la mocedad aprende de la vida. Eso es riguroso, pero también dichoso.
sentences.english: "And what does a son-in-law do?" "A son-in-law helps his mother-in-law, and youth learns from life. That is rigorous, but also happy."

sentences.text: —¿Qué cuestiones se discuten en la mesa? —Las cuestiones del día: el agua, el trabajo, la lluvia que zumbando cae sobre el zinc.
sentences.english: "What questions are discussed at the table?" "The questions of the day: the water, the work, the rain that falls buzzing on the zinc."

sentences.text: —¿Y cómo termina el día de una voluntaria? —La niña, alarmada por la lluvia, corrió a abrazar a su madre. Nadie sabía todo lo que había acontecido, pero se sabía lo importante.
sentences.english: "And how does a volunteer's day end?" "The girl, alarmed by the rain, ran to hug her mother. Nobody knew everything that had happened, but the important thing was known."

sentences.text: —¿Qué se necesita para seguir? —Una admirada paciencia, un poco de literatura y una broma a tiempo: Karla bromeó con todos, y la tarde fue más ligera.
sentences.english: "What is needed to go on?" "An admired patience, a little literature and a joke in time: Karla joked with everybody, and the afternoon was lighter."

sentences.text: —¿Y qué pasó con la tos del joven? —Tosió un rato y se disculpó. Su historia era dolorosa, pero suficiente para entender lo acontecido.
sentences.english: "And what about the young man's cough?" "He coughed for a while and apologized. His story was painful, but enough to understand what had happened."

sentences.text: —¿Quién bromeó para alegrar la noche? —Karla bromeó otra vez, y la admirada paciencia de todos se llenó de risa. Después leyeron literatura en voz alta.
sentences.english: "Who joked to cheer the night?" "Karla joked again, and everyone's admired patience filled with laughter. Afterwards they read literature aloud."

sentences.text: —¿Y la señora de la casa? —Alarmada, salió a la calle a pedir ayuda. Yo sé lo que había acontecido en esa casa, y lo diré cuando me pregunten.
sentences.english: "And the lady of the house?" "Alarmed, she went out into the street to ask for help. I know what had happened in that house, and I will say it when they ask me."

sentences.text: —¿Cómo es la clínica del pueblo? —Excelente. La enfermera es excelente, y el servicio, aunque sencillo, es excelente también.
sentences.english: "What is the town clinic like?" "Excellent. The nurse is excellent, and the service, although simple, is excellent too."
